stem: The following are grounds for legal separation, except:
choices: Adultery
Conviction of a crime involving a penalty of at least 2 years and 1 day
Attempt by the respondent against the life of the petitioner
Drug addiction, whether or not existing at the time of marriage
None of the above
explanation: Art. 55(4) FC requires a 'final judgment sentencing the respondent to imprisonment of more than six years, even if pardoned.' A conviction for a crime carrying a penalty of at least 2 years and 1 day does not meet that threshold, so (b) is the exception. Adultery is sexual infidelity under Art. 55(8). Attempt by the respondent against the life of the petitioner is Art. 55(9). Drug addiction of the respondent is Art. 55(5), and the article does not require that it arise only during the marriage. Compare Art. 46(4), where concealment of drug addiction existing at the time of the marriage is fraud for annulment.

stem: The effects of legal separation are the following, except:
choices: The spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other.
The absolute community or the conjugal partnership shall be dissolved and liquidated.
The offending spouse shall be disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by intestate and testamentary succession.
The custody of the minor children shall be awarded to the innocent spouse, subject to the provisions of Article 213 of this Code.
None of the above.
explanation: Art. 63 FC lists the effects of the decree: (1) the spouses may live separately, but the marriage bonds are not severed; (2) the ACP/CPG is dissolved and liquidated, and the offending spouse forfeits his share of the net profits under Art. 43(2); (3) custody of minor children goes to the innocent spouse, subject to Art. 213; and (4) the offending spouse is disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by INTESTATE succession. Choice (c) wrongly adds 'testamentary' succession. Testamentary provisions in favor of the offending spouse made before the decree are revoked by operation of law. However, the innocent spouse may still validly institute or benefit the offending spouse in a will executed after the decree (Tolentino).

stem: Abandonment of petitioner by respondent for more than one year is a ground for legal separation.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 55(10) FC: the ground is 'abandonment of petitioner by respondent WITHOUT JUSTIFIABLE CAUSE for more than one year.' Abandonment for more than one year is not a ground if it was justified, for example where the spouse left to escape maltreatment (Ong v. Ong; Goitia v. Campos-Rueda). The statement omits the qualifier, so it is not absolutely true.

stem: The offending spouse shall be disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by intestate succession if he gave cause for legal separation.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 63(4) FC makes disqualification from intestate succession an effect of the DECREE of legal separation, not of merely giving cause for it. A spouse who has given cause but against whom no decree has been issued is not disqualified from intestate succession. Contrast Art. 921(4) Civil Code, where merely 'giving cause for legal separation' is enough as a ground for DISINHERITANCE in a will.

stem: A petition for legal separation may be filed on any of the following grounds, except:
choices: Final judgment sentencing the respondent to imprisonment of more than six years;
Contracting by the respondent of a subsequent bigamous marriage, whether in the Philippines or abroad;
Attempt by the respondent against the life of the petitioner;
Abandonment of petitioner by respondent without justifiable cause for more than one year.
None of the above
explanation: All four are grounds under Art. 55 FC. (a) is par. (4), final judgment sentencing respondent to imprisonment of more than six years, even if pardoned. (b) is par. (7), a subsequent bigamous marriage whether in the Philippines or abroad. (c) is par. (9), attempt against the life of the petitioner. (d) is par. (10), abandonment without justifiable cause for more than one year. Hence 'None of the above.' Compare the older version of this item, where choice (c) was altered to add 'a common child, or a child of the petitioner'.

stem: A petition for legal separation may be filed on any of the following grounds, except:
choices: Final judgment sentencing the respondent to imprisonment of more than six years
Contracting by the respondent of a subsequent bigamous marriage, whether in the Philippines or abroad
Attempt by the respondent against the life of the petitioner; a common child, or a child of the petitioner
Abandonment of petitioner by respondent without justifiable cause for more than one year
None of the above
explanation: Art. 55(9) FC covers only an 'attempt by the respondent against the life of the PETITIONER.' Choice (c) adds 'a common child, or a child of the petitioner,' which is not in par. (9). The phrase 'the petitioner, a common child, or a child of the petitioner' appears only in par. (1) (repeated physical violence or grossly abusive conduct) and par. (3) (corruption or inducement to prostitution). Choices (a), (b) and (d) restate pars. (4), (7) and (10), which are grounds. This is Uribe's one-phrase-alteration trap.

stem: The obligation of mutual support between spouses ceases after the following, except:
choices: dissolution of the marriage by the death of a spouse
declaration of nullity
annulment of marriage
legal separation
none of the above
explanation: Art. 198 FC: 'After the final judgment granting the petition [for legal separation, annulment or declaration of nullity], the obligation of MUTUAL support between the spouses ceases. However, in case of legal separation, the court may order that the guilty spouse shall give support to the innocent one.' Death also dissolves the marriage and extinguishes the obligation. After a decree of legal separation, support is no longer mutual. Only a one-sided, court-ordered support from the guilty spouse to the innocent spouse may remain. So mutual support ceases in all four cases, and the answer is (e).
key_note: Note: the Midterm Exam and 'kuya R' samplex keys marked (d) (legal separation). This is incorrect for the 'MUTUAL support' wording: Art. 198 expressly says mutual support ceases after final judgment, and Uribe's 2025 CivRev key marks (e). Answer (d) is correct only for the differently worded item ('the obligation of supporting a spouse').

stem: The obligation of supporting a spouse ceases after the following, except:
choices: Dissolution of the marriage by death of the spouse
Declaration of nullity
Annulment of marriage
Legal separation
None of the above
explanation: This item says 'the obligation of SUPPORTING A SPOUSE,' not mutual support. Under Art. 198 FC, after a decree of legal separation the court may order the guilty spouse to support the innocent one. The obligation to support a spouse therefore does not necessarily cease, because the marriage bond subsists (Art. 63(1)). After death, nullity or annulment, the obligation ceases entirely. The answer is (d). Compare the 'mutual support' version, whose answer is (e).

stem: The decree of legal separation shall have the following effects:
choices: The spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other
The offending spouse shall have no right to any share of the net profits earned by the absolute community or the conjugal partnership
The offending spouse shall be disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by intestate succession
all of the above
none of the above
explanation: All three are effects of the decree under Art. 63 FC. (a) is par. (1), the right to live separately, the marriage bonds not being severed. (b) is par. (2): the ACP/CPG is dissolved and liquidated, and the offending spouse has no right to any share of the net profits, which are forfeited per Art. 43(2). (c) is par. stem: The decree of legal separation shall have the following effects, except:
choices: The marriage bonds shall not be severed;

The absolute community or the conjugal partnership shall be dissolved and liquidated but the offending spouse shall have a share of the net profits earned by the absolute community or the conjugal partnership
Provisions in favor of the offending spouse made in the will of the innocent spouse shall be revoked by operation of law
All of the above
None of the above
explanation: Art. 63(2) FC: the ACP/CPG is dissolved and liquidated, 'but the offending spouse shall have NO right to any share of the net profits,' which are forfeited under Art. 43(2) in favor of the common children. Choice (b) says the opposite, so it is the exception. (a) restates Art. 63(1): the marriage bonds are not severed. (c) restates the second sentence of Art. 63(4): testamentary provisions in favor of the offending spouse are revoked by operation of law.

stem: In order for a petition for legal separation to prosper, the ground must have arisen only during the marriage.
choices: True
False
explanation: Disagree. Art. 55 FC generally contemplates acts during the marriage, but some grounds are not limited by time of origin. Drug addiction, habitual alcoholism, lesbianism or homosexuality of the respondent (Art. 55(5)-(6)) are grounds even if they already existed at the time of the celebration. If such a condition existed then and was concealed, it may ALSO be a ground for annulment by fraud (Art. 46(4)).

stem: It is possible for the same facts to constitute both a ground for legal separation and a ground for annulment of the marriage.
choices: True
False
explanation: Yes. For example, drug addiction or homosexuality existing at the time of the marriage and concealed is fraud for annulment (Arts. 45(3), 46(4) FC), and the same condition is a ground for legal separation (Art. 55(5)-(6)). The client may choose. Annulment severs the bond and allows remarriage. Legal separation preserves the bond, so there is no remarriage, but the possibility of reconciliation remains and the guilty spouse may be ordered to give support (Art. 198).

stem: A and B, Filipinos, were married in Cotabato City. A went to Saudi Arabia, converted to Islam, and married another Filipina there. For B's petition for legal separation, it matters whether the subsequent marriage is valid under Philippine law.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 55(7) FC makes 'contracting by the respondent of a subsequent bigamous marriage, whether in the Philippines or abroad' a ground. The ground lies in the act of contracting the subsequent marriage while the first subsists. The petitioner need not prove whether that second marriage is valid or void, under Philippine law or the law of the place where it was celebrated. Conversion to Islam does not entitle a spouse married under civil law to contract another marriage, and the petitioner may sue regardless. Uribe: 'the spouse will always be allowed to file for legal separation whether or not the second marriage is valid.'

stem: A petition for legal separation was filed. 4 weeks after filing, the court scheduled this case for a hearing. Is it proper for the court to do so?
choices: It depends on the purpose: the court cannot proceed to trial within the cooling-off period, but it can hear motions for provisional remedies such as support
Yes, the court may proceed to trial at any time after filing
No, the court cannot conduct any hearing at all within six months from filing
Yes, provided the respondent consents to an early trial
explanation: Art. 58 FC: 'An action for legal separation shall in no case be TRIED before six months shall have elapsed since the filing of the petition.' What is barred is trial on the merits during the cooling-off period. The court may hear and act on incidental matters, such as support pendente lite, custody of the children and administration of property (Arts. 49, 61, 62). In Araneta v. Concepcion, the cooling-off period does not override the provisions on custody and support pendente lite, and Somosa-Ramos v. Vamenta allowed hearing a motion for preliminary injunction. Note that under RA 9262 Sec. 19, Art. 58 does not apply where VAWC violence is alleged.

stem: Where the spouses executed a notarized agreement allowing each other to get concubines, a petition for legal separation on the ground of sexual infidelity will prosper.
choices: True
False
explanation: The petition will not prosper because of CONSENT (Art. 56(2) FC). The spouses' agreement allowing each other to have paramours, though void as contrary to morals, shows consent given in advance to the commission of the offense (People v. Schneckenberger). It is consent, not condonation, because it was given before the act. Condonation is forgiveness of an act already committed. The proper ground in the petition would have been sexual infidelity under Art. 55(8), but the defense bars the decree.

stem: Recrimination as a defense in legal separation requires that the offense committed by the petitioner be similar to the offense charged against the respondent.
choices: True
False
explanation: No. Recrimination, or mutual guilt (Art. 56(4) FC: 'where both parties have given ground for legal separation'), does not require that the spouses' offenses be of the same kind. For example, the husband's sexual infidelity can be set up against the wife's attempt on his life (Bar 2006, Saul and Cecile). The principle is that one must come to court with clean hands, and it does not matter who offended first (Tolentino).

stem: Respondent admitted guilt and the acts as alleged in the complaint. Thereafter, the court granted the petition for legal separation. This is proper so long as there was other evidence presented to support the petition, apart from the admission.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 60 FC: 'No decree of legal separation shall be based upon a stipulation of facts or a confession of judgment,' and the prosecutor must take steps to prevent collusion and ensure that evidence is not fabricated or suppressed. Ocampo v. Florenciano: what the law prohibits is a judgment based EXCLUSIVELY or mainly on the confession. If the petitioner presents independent evidence proving the ground, the decree may be granted even if the respondent admitted the offense.

stem: Upon a decree of legal separation, the wife is required to revert to her maiden name.
choices: True
False
explanation: No. Legal separation does not sever the marriage bond (Art. 63(1) FC). Under Art. 372 Civil Code, when legal separation has been granted, the wife shall continue using her name and surname employed before the legal separation. Laperal v. Republic calls this language mandatory, because her married status is unaffected.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. An action for legal separation shall be filed within one year from the time the innocent spouse became cognizant of the cause.
2. If the husband does not actively look for the wife who left the conjugal home after her adulterous acts were discovered, there is condonation.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Art. 57 FC: the action 'shall be filed within FIVE YEARS from the time of the OCCURRENCE of the cause.' The one-year-from-knowledge period was under the old Civil Code (Art. 102) and was not retained. No. 2 is FALSE. Condonation (Art. 56(1)) is forgiveness, express or implied, of the offense with knowledge of it, for example by voluntary cohabitation or sexual relations afterward (Ginez v. Bugayong). The husband's mere failure to search for the wife who left after her infidelity was discovered does not show forgiveness. Compare People v. Sensano, where a husband's long absence despite knowledge was treated as consent for purposes of the criminal action.

statements: 1. The spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other only from the time the decree of legal separation becomes final and executory.
2. The offending spouse shall be disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by intestate succession if he gave cause for legal separation
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Art. 61 FC: 'AFTER THE FILING of the petition for legal separation, the spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other.' The right does not wait for the decree to become final. No. 2 is FALSE. Disqualification from intestate succession under Art. 63(4) is an effect of the DECREE, not of merely giving cause. stem: The decree of legal separation shall entitle the spouses to live separately from each other as the marriage bond shall be severed.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 63(1) FC: the spouses are entitled to live separately, 'BUT THE MARRIAGE BONDS SHALL NOT BE SEVERED.' Legal separation is only a relative divorce (a mensa et thoro). The spouses remain married and cannot remarry, and the duty of fidelity continues.

stem: The decree of legal separation shall entitle the spouses to live separately from each other, but the marriage bonds shall not be severed.
choices: True
False
explanation: As printed, this is the verbatim text of Art. 63(1) FC: the decree entitles the spouses to live separately, but the marriage bonds are not severed. Note, however, that under Art. 61 the right to live separately already arises upon the FILING of the petition, and the decree confirms it.
key_note: The printed key said TRUE. A handwritten correction says 'FALSE, Art. 61' with 'after the filing of the petition' inserted, apparently for an altered version. As worded, the codal statement is true. If Uribe's version says the right arises only 'upon the finality of the decree,' it is false (see the next item).

stem: The following will dissolve both the absolute community and the marriage, except:
choices: Death of one of the spouses.
Annulment of the marriage.
Legal separation.
All of the above.
None of the above.
explanation: Death (Arts. 99(1), 126(1) FC) and annulment (Arts. 99(3), 126(3)) dissolve both the marriage and the property regime. A decree of legal separation dissolves the ACP or CPG (Arts. 63(2), 99(2), 126(2)) but does NOT sever the marriage bond (Art. 63(1)). Legal separation is therefore the exception.

stem: A petition for legal separation may be filed on this ground:
choices: Grossly abusive conduct directed against a common child, or a child of the respondent;
Attempt of petitioner to corrupt or induce a common child to engage in prostitution
Conviction by final judgement of a crime involving moral turpitude
All of the above
None of the above
explanation: Each choice alters Art. 55 FC. (a): par. (1) speaks of grossly abusive conduct against 'the petitioner, a common child, or a child of the PETITIONER,' not a child of the respondent. (b): par. (3) speaks of an attempt of the RESPONDENT, not the petitioner, to corrupt or induce to prostitution. (c): par. (4) requires a final judgment sentencing the respondent to imprisonment of more than six years, not merely conviction of a crime involving moral turpitude. None is a ground.

stem: Saul, a married man, had an adulterous relation with Tessie. In one of the trysts, Saul's wife, Cecile, caught them in flagrante. Armed with a gun, Cecile shot Saul in a fit of extreme jealousy, nearly killing him. Four (4) years after the incident, Saul filed an action for legal separation against Cecile on the ground that she attempted to kill him. If you were the judge, how will you decide the case?
choices: Grant the petition; attempt on the life of a spouse is a ground and no criminal conviction is needed.
Grant the petition, since it was filed within five years.
Deny the petition; Saul is not an aggrieved spouse – both parties gave ground for legal separation (recrimination), and the attempt was impelled by passion.
Deny the petition because Cecile was not convicted.
explanation: Deny the petition. Saul's argument is that attempt against the life of the petitioner is a ground under Art. 55(9) FC, that no criminal conviction is required, and that the action was filed within five years (Art. 57). But Saul himself committed sexual infidelity (Art. 55(8)). Under Art. 56(4), the petition shall be denied 'where both parties have given ground for legal separation.' This is recrimination, or mutual guilt, and the party who seeks relief must come to court with clean hands. The bar answer also notes that the attempt must be intentional and wrongful, while Cecile acted in a fit of extreme jealousy upon catching Saul in flagrante. Prescription is not an issue because only four years had passed.

stem: Saul, a married man, had an adulterous relation with Tessie. In one of the trysts, Saul's wife, Cecile, caught them in flagrante. Armed with a gun, Cecile shot Saul in a fit of extreme jealousy, nearly killing him. Four (4) years after the incident, Saul filed an action for legal separation against Cecile on the ground that she attempted to kill him. If you were the lawyer of Cecile, what would be your best defense?
choices: Prescription, because the action was filed more than one year after the incident
Recrimination or mutual guilt, because Saul himself committed sexual infidelity
Condonation, because Saul did not file a criminal case
Lack of a prior criminal conviction for attempted or frustrated parricide
Collusion between the spouses
explanation: Cecile's best defense is recrimination, or mutual guilt (Art. 56(4) FC): Saul himself gave ground for legal separation through his adulterous relationship, which is sexual infidelity under Art. 55(8). Prescription fails because the action was filed four years after the incident, within the five years of Art. 57. There is no condonation, consent or collusion on these facts. Lack of a criminal conviction is no defense, since Art. 55(9) does not require one.

stem: Why would one spouse choose legal separation [instead of annulment or declaration of nullity]?
choices: Because the spouse still wants support from the other spouse (the marriage bond is retained)
Because legal separation allows the spouses to remarry
Because legal separation has no prescriptive period
Because legal separation may be granted on a stipulation of facts
explanation: Legal separation keeps the marriage bond (Art. 63(1) FC). After the decree the court may order the guilty spouse to support the innocent one (Art. 198), and the spouses may still reconcile (Arts. 65-66). (b) is wrong: neither spouse may remarry. (c) is wrong: the action prescribes in five years (Art. 57). (d) is wrong: no decree may be based on a stipulation of facts (Art. 60). Uribe's recitation answer: 'You still want support from the other spouse.'

stem: Legal separation is a kind of divorce which is relative.
choices: True
False
explanation: Legal separation is a relative or limited divorce, a mensa et thoro (from bed and board). The spouses may live apart and their property regime is dissolved, but the marriage bond subsists (Art. 63(1) FC). An absolute divorce, a vinculo matrimonii, severs the bond. Republic v. Quintos describes legal separation under the old Spanish law in these terms.

stem: The Family Code consistently refers to legal separation only as a 'petition' and never as an 'action'.
choices: True
False
explanation: The Family Code uses the terms interchangeably. Art. 55 speaks of 'a PETITION for legal separation,' while Arts. 57 and 58 speak of 'an ACTION for legal separation' (Art. 58: 'action ... since the filing of the petition'). Uribe: 'The law is confused because it refers to petition or action interchangeably.'

stem: Sps. A and B. A filed a petition for legal separation on the ground that B was found guilty of a crime. The defense raised by B was that he was not imprisoned because he was able to avail of the probation law. The petition will prosper.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 55(4) FC requires a 'final judgment sentencing the respondent to imprisonment of MORE THAN SIX YEARS.' Under the Probation Law (PD 968 Sec. 9(a), as amended by RA 10707), offenders sentenced to a maximum term of imprisonment of more than six years cannot apply for probation. Since B was granted probation, his sentence did not exceed six years, so the ground does not exist.

stem: A lawyer notarized an agreement between spouses that they are allowed to get concubines etc. Thereafter, a petition for legal separation was filed against the other spouse. In relation to the document, what could be the ground?
choices: Sexual infidelity
Repeated physical violence
Abandonment without justifiable cause for more than one year
Attempt to corrupt or induce the petitioner to engage in prostitution
explanation: The agreement allowing the spouses to keep paramours relates to SEXUAL INFIDELITY, a ground under Art. 55(8) FC. As the next recitation item shows, such an agreement, though void, amounts to consent to the infidelity, and the petition would be denied under Art. 56(2).

stem: Consent is with respect to acts that have already been committed, while condonation is with respect to future acts.
choices: True
False
explanation: The statement reverses the concepts. CONSENT (Art. 56(2) FC) is agreement given BEFORE the commission of the offense, for future acts. CONDONATION (Art. 56(1)) is forgiveness of an offense ALREADY COMMITTED. Uribe: 'Consent is with respect to future actions. Condonation is with respect to acts that have already been committed.'

stem: If a spouse, having knowledge of a ground for legal separation (sexual infidelity), had sexual relations with the guilty spouse, it is possible that this will not amount to condonation.
choices: True
False
explanation: Condonation (Art. 56(1) FC) requires intent to forgive, with knowledge of the offense. Ginez v. Bugayong held that a single voluntary act of marital intercourse after knowledge of the offense is ORDINARILY sufficient to constitute condonation. 'Ordinarily' leaves room for exceptions. Tolentino cites Hawkins v. Hawkins: a wife who, for the children's sake and in an effort at reconciliation, cohabited with the husband for one night did not condone. So it is possible that sexual relations do not amount to condonation.
key_note: The general rule (Bugayong) leans toward condonation. TRUE here only because the statement asks whether it is POSSIBLE that it will not amount to condonation.

stem: A petition for legal separation was filed in December 2018, but the acts alleged in the complaint were committed by the respondent in 2011, 2012 and January 2013. The petition will prosper.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 57 FC: the action must be filed within five years from the OCCURRENCE of the cause. Each act is a separate ground with its own five-year period. Acts committed in 2011, 2012 and January 2013 prescribed in 2016, 2017 and January 2018 respectively, so all had prescribed by December 2018. Uribe's answer: 'No. Within 5 years prescription period.'

src: QuAMTO – 2007 Bar; UP BOC – 2007 Bar; Uribe recitation question
stem: If a man commits several acts of sexual infidelity, particularly in 2002, 2003, 2004, 2005, the prescriptive period to file for legal separation runs from 2002.
choices: True
False
explanation: Each act of sexual infidelity is a separate ground, not one continuing offense. Under Art. 57 FC, the five-year period runs from the occurrence of EACH act: from 2002 for the 2002 infidelity, from 2003 for the 2003 infidelity, and so on. The action based on the 2005 act may be filed until 2010. Compare People v. Zapata: each adulterous act is a distinct crime.

stem: A decree of legal separation is required for the disinheritance of a spouse who has given cause for legal separation to be valid.
choices: True
False
explanation: No. Art. 921(4) Civil Code makes it a sufficient cause to disinherit a spouse 'when the spouse has GIVEN CAUSE for legal separation.' No decree is required. Contrast Art. 63(4) FC, where disqualification from intestate succession and revocation of testamentary provisions by operation of law require a DECREE of legal separation.

stem: If drug addiction, habitual alcoholism, lesbianism or homosexuality should occur only during the marriage, would these constitute grounds for a declaration of nullity or for legal separation, or would they render the marriage voidable?
choices: Grounds for declaration of nullity under Art. 36.
Grounds for annulment under Arts. 45-46.
Grounds for legal separation under Art. 55 only; not grounds for nullity or annulment.
Not grounds for any remedy.
explanation: If these conditions arise only DURING the marriage, they are grounds for legal separation (Art. 55(5)-(6) FC). They are not grounds for declaration of nullity, because psychological incapacity under Art. 36 must exist at the time of the celebration (juridical antecedence), and the conditions themselves are not psychological incapacity. Nor do they make the marriage voidable, because fraud under Arts. 45(3) and 46(4) requires concealment of a condition existing at the time of the marriage.

stem: Which of the following remedies, i.e., (a) declaration of nullity of marriage, (b) annulment of marriage, (c) legal separation, and/or (d) separation of property, can an aggrieved spouse avail himself/herself of: If the wife goes abroad to work as a nurse and refuses to come home after the expiration of her three-year contract there.
choices: Legal separation immediately upon expiration of the contract.
Declaration of nullity on the ground of psychological incapacity.
Judicial separation of property after 3 months of refusal; legal separation if the refusal (abandonment without justifiable cause) lasts more than one year from expiration of the contract.
Annulment of marriage.
explanation: During the three-year contract the wife's absence is justified, so no intention to abandon can be presumed. If she fails to return for three months after the contract expires, she is prima facie presumed to have abandoned the family (Art. 101, 3rd par., FC), and the husband may petition for judicial separation of property (Arts. 101, 135(4)). If the refusal continues for more than one year from expiration, he may sue for legal separation for abandonment without justifiable cause for more than one year (Art. 55(10)).

stem: Which of the following remedies, i.e., (a) declaration of nullity of marriage, (b) annulment of marriage, (c) legal separation, and/or (d) separation of property, can an aggrieved spouse avail himself/herself of: If the husband has a serious affair with his secretary and refuses to stop notwithstanding advice from relatives and friends.
choices: Annulment of marriage only
Declaration of nullity only
Legal separation and/or judicial separation of property
None
explanation: The wife may file for legal separation on the ground of sexual infidelity (Art. 55(8) FC). She may also file for judicial separation of property for the husband's failure to comply with his marital obligation of fidelity (Art. 135(4) in relation to Arts. 68, 101). Infidelity arising during the marriage is not a ground for nullity or annulment (Dedel v. CA: sexual infidelity per se is a ground for legal separation, not psychological incapacity).

stem: Which of the following remedies, i.e., (a) declaration of nullity of marriage, (b) annulment of marriage, (c) legal separation, and/or (d) separation of property, can an aggrieved spouse avail himself/herself of: If the husband beats up his wife every time he comes home drunk.
choices: Annulment of marriage on the ground of force
None, unless he is convicted of physical injuries
Legal separation, judicial separation of property, and declaration of nullity if it constitutes psychological incapacity existing at the time of marriage
Declaration of nullity only
explanation: Repeated physical violence against the petitioner is a ground for legal separation (Art. 55(1) FC). Failure to observe mutual respect is ground for judicial separation of property (Art. 135(4) in relation to Arts. 68, 101). If the violent behavior manifests a psychological incapacity existing at the time of the celebration, declaration of nullity under Art. 36 is possible. No criminal conviction is required for Art. 55(1). 'Force' under Art. 45(4) refers to force used to obtain consent to the marriage, so it does not apply.

stem: Under what conditions may drug addiction be a ground for legal separation between the spouses?
choices: There must be no condonation or consent, the action must be filed within 5 years from the occurrence of the cause, and the addiction arises during the marriage.
The drug addiction must have been concealed at the time of the marriage.
The addiction must be grave, antecedent and incurable.
The action must be filed within 5 years from the celebration of the marriage.
explanation: For drug addiction to support a decree of legal separation: (1) it must be the respondent's addiction (Art. 55(5) FC); (2) there must be no condonation of or consent to it (Art. 56); and (3) the action must be filed within five years from the occurrence of the cause (Art. 57). (b) and (c) mix up the requisites for annulment by fraud (Art. 46(4)) and for psychological incapacity (Art. 36). (d) counts the period from the wrong date.
key_note: The bar answer lists 'the addiction arises during the marriage' as a condition. Uribe's quizzes treat drug addiction 'whether or not existing at the time of marriage' as a ground (see the 'grounds, except' item). Choose (a) as the best answer, but remember that Art. 55(5) has no time qualifier.

stem: After they got married, Nikki discovered that Christian was having an affair with another woman. But Nikki decided to give it a try and lived with him for two (2) years. After two (2) years, Nikki filed an action for legal separation on the ground of Christian’s sexual infidelity. Will the action prosper?
choices: Yes, because the action was filed within five years from the occurrence of the cause.
No, because the action has prescribed.
No, because Nikki's decision to live with Christian after discovering the affair amounts to condonation – unless the affair is still continuing, since every act of infidelity is a separate ground.
Yes, because condonation must be in writing.
explanation: Under Art. 56(1) FC, the petition shall be denied where the aggrieved party has condoned the offense. Condonation may be implied, and Nikki's decision to live with Christian for two years with knowledge of the affair amounts to condonation (Ginez v. Bugayong). The action has not prescribed, since five years have not run (Art. 57). However, if the affair continued after the condonation, each new act of infidelity is a separate ground that was not condoned.
key_note: The answer covers the original affair only. Later acts of infidelity would be new grounds.

stem: Rosa and Ariel were married in the Catholic Church of Tarlac, Tarlac on 05 Jan. 1988. In 1990, Ariel went to Saudi Arabia to work. There, after being converted into Islam, Ariel married Mystica. Rosa learned of the second marriage of Ariel on 01 Jan. 1992 when Ariel returned to the Philippines with Mystica. Rosa filed an action for legal separation on 05 Feb. 1994. Does Rosa have legal grounds to ask for legal separation?
choices: Yes, Ariel's abandonment for more than one year (and his subsequent bigamous marriage) are grounds for legal separation.
No, because Ariel's conversion to Islam allowed him to marry another wife.
No, because her only remedy is a declaration of nullity of the second marriage.
No, because the grounds occurred abroad.
explanation: Yes. Ariel contracted a subsequent bigamous marriage abroad, a ground under Art. 55(7) FC 'whether in the Philippines or abroad.' His conversion to Islam does not authorize a second marriage while his civil/Catholic marriage to Rosa subsists. He also abandoned Rosa without justifiable cause for more than one year (Art. 55(10)). The bar suggested answer cites abandonment. Art. 55(7) is the more direct ground.
key_note: The bar answer relies on abandonment. The bigamous marriage under Art. 55(7) is equally, and more directly, a ground.

stem: Rosa and Ariel were married in the Catholic Church of Tarlac, Tarlac on 05 Jan. 1988. In 1990, Ariel went to Saudi Arabia to work. There, after being converted into Islam, Ariel married Mystica. Rosa learned of the second marriage of Ariel on 01 Jan. 1992 when Ariel returned to the Philippines with Mystica. Rosa filed an action for legal separation on 05 Feb. 1994. Has the action prescribed?
choices: Yes, because more than five years had elapsed from the celebration of the marriage in 1988.
No, because the action was filed within five years from the occurrence of the cause, which could not have been earlier than 1990.
Yes, because it should have been filed within one year from discovery on 01 Jan. 1992.
No, because an action for legal separation is imprescriptible.
explanation: No. Under Art. 57 FC, the action must be filed within five years from the OCCURRENCE of the cause, not from the celebration of the marriage or from discovery. Ariel's subsequent marriage in Saudi Arabia could not have taken place earlier than 1990, when he left. Rosa therefore had at least until 1995, and her February 1994 filing was timely.

src: QuAMTO – 2011 Bar; UP BOC – 2011 Bar MCQ
stem: The wife filed a case of legal separation against her husband on the ground of sexual infidelity without previously exerting earnest efforts to come to a compromise with him. The judge dismissed the case for having been filed without complying with a condition precedent. Is the dismissal proper?
choices: No, efforts at a compromise will only deepen the wife's anguish.
No, since legal separation like validity of marriage is not subject to compromise agreement for purposes of filing.
Yes, to avoid a family feud that is hurtful to everyone.
Yes, since the dispute could have been settled with the parties agreeing to legal separation.
explanation: Earnest efforts toward a compromise between family members are generally a condition precedent to suits between them (Art. 151 FC). This requirement does not apply to matters that cannot be the subject of compromise. Under Art. 2035 Civil Code, there can be no compromise on the validity of a marriage or on legal separation. Dismissal on that ground is therefore improper. Do not confuse this with Art. 59, under which the COURT must take steps toward reconciliation before decreeing legal separation.

src: QuAMTO – 2011 Bar; UP BOC – 2011 Bar MCQ
stem: No decree of legal separation can be issued
choices: Unless the children's welfare is attended to first.
Without prior efforts at reconciliation shown to be futile.
Unless the court first directs mediation of the parties.
Without prior investigation conducted by a public prosecutor.
explanation: Art. 59 FC: 'No legal separation may be decreed unless the Court has taken steps toward the reconciliation of the spouses and is fully satisfied, despite such efforts, that reconciliation is highly improbable.' Choice (d) misstates Art. 60, which requires the court to order the prosecutor to take steps to prevent collusion and suppression or fabrication of evidence. (a) and (c) are not requisites under the law.

stem: In legal separation, which is not correct?
choices: The aggrieved spouse may file the action within five (5) years from the time of the occurrence of the cause.
No trial shall be held without the 6-month cooling off period being observed.
The spouses will be entitled to live separately upon the start of the trial.
The prosecuting attorney has to conduct his own investigation.
explanation: Under Art. 61 FC, the spouses are entitled to live separately 'after the FILING of the petition,' not upon the start of trial, so (C) is incorrect. (A) restates Art. 57. (B) restates Art. 58. (D) is correct: under Art. 60 the court orders the prosecuting attorney to take steps to prevent collusion and to see that evidence is not fabricated or suppressed, and the Rule on Legal Separation (A.M. No. 02-11-11-SC) requires the prosecutor to investigate and report on collusion.
key_note: Note: the UP BOC suggested answer was (D). This is incorrect because Art. 60 and A.M. No. 02-11-11-SC do require the prosecutor to investigate collusion, while (C) misstates Art. 61.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. Under the Family Code, sexual infidelity of either the husband or the wife is a ground for legal separation, even if the husband's act does not constitute concubinage as defined in the Revised Penal Code.
2. A civil action for legal separation based on concubinage may proceed only after the conviction of the defendant spouse in the criminal case for concubinage.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: Art. 55(8) FC. Tolentino: under the Family Code, sexual intercourse of either spouse with another person is a ground because it is infidelity, although the husband's act may not amount to concubinage under the RPC. This equalizes husband and wife. No. 1 is TRUE. No. 2 is FALSE: a civil action for legal separation based on concubinage may proceed ahead of, or simultaneously with, the criminal action. It is not an action to enforce civil liability arising from the offense; it seeks the right to live separately and its consequences (Gandionco v. Peñaranda).

stem: Which of the following is a valid ground for legal separation under Article 55(9) (attempt by the respondent against the life of the petitioner)?
choices: H, acting in legitimate defense against the unlawful aggression of W, inflicted serious wounds on W
H inflicted slight physical injuries on W once, without intent to kill
H, with intent to kill, poisoned W's food, but W survived due to timely medical attention
All of the above
None of the above
explanation: Art. 55(9) FC. Tolentino: an attempt against the life of the petitioner implies INTENT TO KILL, so the act must amount to attempted or frustrated parricide. Mere infliction of physical injuries without intent to kill is not enough under par. (9), though repeated physical violence falls under par. (1). A justified act, such as self-defense against the other spouse's unlawful aggression, is not wrongful and is no ground. Only (c) qualifies. No criminal conviction is needed.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. Sexual perversion committed by free mutual agreement of the spouses entitles either of them to ask for legal separation.
2. Abandonment of petitioner by respondent without justifiable cause for more than one year is a ground for legal separation.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Tolentino: sexual perversion as a ground (Art. 55(8) FC) implies coercion by the respondent to make the petitioner submit. If the perversion is by free mutual agreement, both are equally guilty and neither may ask for legal separation (see also Art. 56(2)-(4)). No. 2 is TRUE: it is the verbatim text of Art. 55(10). Abandonment means leaving without intent to return.

stem: W discovered H's affair with X. For the sake of their children, and in an effort at reconciliation, W cohabited with H for one night in a hotel. The reconciliation failed and W filed for legal separation. H raised the defense of condonation. Following Tolentino, the defense:
choices: Will not prosper, because that single cohabitation in an effort at reconciliation does not amount to condonation
Will prosper, because condonation need not be express
Will prosper, because any cohabitation after knowledge of the offense is implied condonation
Will not prosper, because condonation must always be in writing
None of the above
explanation: Art. 56(1) FC. Condonation may be express or implied. Implied condonation requires that the injured spouse, with clear knowledge of the offense, deliberately cohabit with the offender, showing a clear intent to forgive. Tolentino cites Hawkins v. Hawkins: a wife's single night of cohabitation with her husband in a hotel, for the children's sake and in an effort at reconciliation, was held not to be condonation. Compare Ginez v. Bugayong, where voluntary intercourse on two nights after knowledge was held to be condonation.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. Consent is unilateral, or an act of only one spouse, while connivance implies agreement, express or implied, by both spouses to the ground for legal separation.
2. A husband who, suspecting his wife of adultery, pretended to go away for the night but returned and caught her in adultery, is guilty of connivance and cannot obtain legal separation.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: Art. 56(2)-(3) FC. No. 1 is TRUE. Tolentino: consent is the act of one spouse agreeing in advance to the commission of the act, while connivance implies agreement, express or implied, by BOTH spouses. No. 2 is FALSE. Merely giving a suspected spouse the opportunity to indulge an existing adulterous disposition, without actively participating, is not connivance. The husband who pretended to leave for the night and caught the wife was not guilty of connivance.

stem: H suspected W of infidelity. He hired a private detective to gather evidence. The detective, on his own initiative, lured W into an act of sexual infidelity with him. H then filed a petition for legal separation. The petition should be:
choices: Granted, because sexual infidelity was proved
Denied, on the ground of connivance
Granted, because H did not authorize the detective to commit the act
Denied, on the ground of recrimination
None of the above
explanation: Art. 56(3) FC. Tolentino: the husband must not actively participate in bringing about the misconduct by providing the opportunity, directly or through an agent. If his agent, here the detective, brings about the adultery, the husband is chargeable with connivance even if he did not authorize the agent to do so. The petition is denied.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. If the petitioner dies during the pendency of the action for legal separation, the action survives and may be continued by the heirs.
2. Where both parties have given ground for legal separation, the petition shall be denied.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. An action for legal separation is purely personal. The death of either party abates the action, which cannot be continued by the heirs (Lapuz-Sy v. Eufemio, 43 SCRA 177: actio personalis moritur cum persona). No. 2 is TRUE: it is Art. 56(4) FC (recrimination or mutual guilt). One who seeks relief must come with clean hands, and it does not matter who offended first or who is more guilty.

stem: W had an affair in March 2018. H discovered it only in January 2022 and filed a petition for legal separation in December 2023. The action:
choices: Has not prescribed, because it was filed within five years from H's discovery of the cause
Has not prescribed, because it was filed within two years from discovery
Is imprescriptible
Has prescribed, because it was not filed within five years from the occurrence of the cause
None of the above
explanation: Art. 57 FC: the action must be filed within five years from the OCCURRENCE of the cause. Discovery is irrelevant, since the Civil Code's one-year-from-knowledge period was not retained. Five years from March 2018 expired in March 2023, so the December 2023 petition is barred by prescription (Art. 56(6)).

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. An action for legal separation shall in no case be tried before six months shall have elapsed since the filing of the petition; during this period the court cannot act on custody of the children or support pendente lite.
2. No decree of legal separation shall be based upon a stipulation of facts or a confession of judgment.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. The first clause is Art. 58 FC, but the cooling-off period does not prevent the court from determining custody, support pendente lite and other incidental matters (Art. 62 in relation to Art. 49; Araneta v. Concepcion). No. 2 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 60, first paragraph. The prosecutor must also take steps to prevent collusion and to ensure that evidence is not fabricated or suppressed.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. The decree of legal separation dissolves the marriage bond, so that the obligation of mutual fidelity ceases.

2. The offending spouse shall be disqualified from inheriting from the innocent spouse by intestate succession, and provisions in favor of the offending spouse made in the will of the innocent spouse shall be revoked by operation of law.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Art. 63(1) FC: the marriage bonds are NOT severed. The duty of fidelity therefore subsists, and adultery or concubinage committed after the decree is still punishable (Tolentino). No. 2 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 63(4). Testamentary provisions in favor of the offending spouse made before the decree are revoked ipso jure. A will made by the innocent spouse after the decree in favor of the offender is valid.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. After the finality of the decree of legal separation, the donations made by the innocent spouse in favor of the offending spouse are revoked by operation of law.
2. The innocent spouse may revoke the designation of the offending spouse as beneficiary in any insurance policy, even if such designation be stipulated as irrevocable.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: Art. 64 FC. No. 1 is FALSE. Revocation of donations is NOT by operation of law; the innocent spouse 'MAY revoke' them, within five years from finality of the decree. Contrast Art. 63(4), under which testamentary provisions are revoked by operation of law. No. 2 is TRUE: the innocent spouse may revoke the insurance beneficiary designation 'even if such designation be stipulated as irrevocable.' The revocation takes effect upon written notification to the insured.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. If the spouses reconcile, a corresponding joint manifestation under oath duly signed by them shall be filed with the court in the same proceeding for legal separation.
2. Upon reconciliation after the decree of legal separation has become final, the former property regime of the spouses is automatically revived.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 65 FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Under Art. 66(2), the final decree is set aside, but the separation of property and any forfeiture of the guilty spouse's share already effected SUBSIST, unless the spouses agree to revive their former regime. That agreement must be under oath, comply with Art. 67 and be approved by the court after notice to creditors. Revival is not automatic.

stem: Which of the following is NOT an effect of the filing of a petition for legal separation, or of its pendency?
choices: The spouses shall be entitled to live separately from each other
In the absence of a written agreement between the spouses, the court shall designate either of them or a third person to administer the absolute community or conjugal partnership property
The obligation of mutual fidelity between the spouses ceases
The court shall provide for the support of the spouses and the custody and support of the common children, in the absence of adequate written agreement
None of the above
explanation: Arts. 61, 62 and 49 FC. Upon filing, the spouses may live separately, and the court, absent a written agreement, designates either spouse or a third person to administer the ACP/CPG with a guardian's powers (Art. 61). It also provides for support of the spouses and custody and support of the common children (Art. 62 in relation to Art. 49). The duty of fidelity does NOT cease, because even the decree does not sever the marriage bond (Art. 63(1)).

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. A single act of physical violence by the respondent to compel the petitioner to change her political affiliation is a ground for legal separation.
2. A single act of physical violence by the respondent directed against a child of the petitioner is a ground for legal separation.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE. Art. 55(2) FC: 'Physical violence or moral pressure to compel the petitioner to change religious or political affiliation.' The paragraph does not require repetition, so a single act of violence for that purpose suffices. No. 2 is FALSE. Art. 55(1) requires 'REPEATED physical violence or grossly abusive conduct' directed against the petitioner, a common child, or a child of the petitioner. A single act of physical violence is not, by itself, the codal ground; it qualifies only if it independently amounts to grossly abusive conduct, so the statement is not absolutely true.

stem: Which of the following is a ground for legal separation?
choices: The respondent's attempt to induce his niece to engage in prostitution
The respondent's connivance in the inducement of the petitioner's adopted child (from her prior marriage) to engage in prostitution
The respondent's attempt to induce his own child by a previous relationship to engage in prostitution
All of the above
None of the above
explanation: Art. 55(3) FC: 'Attempt of respondent to corrupt or induce the petitioner, a common child, or a child of the petitioner, to engage in prostitution, OR CONNIVANCE in such corruption or inducement.' The last paragraph of Art. 55 provides that 'child' includes a child by nature or by adoption. (b) is the respondent's connivance in the inducement of the petitioner's adopted child, so it is a ground. (a) and (c) involve persons who are neither the petitioner, a common child, nor a child of the petitioner.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. Final judgment sentencing the respondent to imprisonment of more than six years is a ground for legal separation, unless the respondent has been pardoned.
2. Lesbianism of the respondent is a ground for legal separation, while concealment of lesbianism existing at the time of the marriage is a ground for annulment.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Art. 55(4) FC: 'Final judgment sentencing the respondent to imprisonment of more than six years, EVEN IF PARDONED.' A pardon does not remove the ground. No. 2 is TRUE. Lesbianism or homosexuality of the respondent is a ground for legal separation (Art. 55(6)), and concealment of lesbianism or homosexuality existing at the time of the marriage is fraud that makes the marriage voidable (Arts. 45(3), 46(4)). Almelor v. RTC: homosexuality per se is only a ground for legal separation; its concealment is what supports annulment.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. In an action for legal separation, the Court shall order the prosecuting attorney or fiscal assigned to it to take steps to prevent collusion between the parties and to take care that the evidence is not fabricated or suppressed.
2. If the respondent fails to file an answer, the court may declare him in default and render judgment granting legal separation on the basis of the petitioner's evidence.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 60, second paragraph, FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Because no decree may be based on a stipulation of facts or confession of judgment (Art. 60), and the State has an interest in preserving marriage, default is not allowed in legal separation (Pacete v. Carriaga). If the respondent does not answer, the court orders the prosecutor to investigate whether there is collusion, and the petitioner must still prove the ground.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. After the filing of the petition for legal separation, the court, in the absence of a written agreement between the spouses, shall designate either of them or a third person to administer the absolute community or conjugal partnership property.
2. The administrator so appointed by the court shall have the same powers and duties as those of a receiver under the Rules of Court.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is Art. 61, second sentence, FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Art. 61, last sentence: 'The administrator appointed by the court shall have the same powers and duties as those of a GUARDIAN under the Rules of Court,' not a receiver.

stem: H obtained a decree of legal separation against W on the ground of her sexual infidelity. Their only child is 5 years old. Under Article 63(3), custody of the child must be awarded to H, the innocent spouse.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 63(3) FC awards custody of the minor children to the innocent spouse 'SUBJECT TO the provisions of Article 213.' Under Art. 213, no child under seven years of age shall be separated from the mother unless the court finds compelling reasons. The mother's sexual infidelity alone is not automatically a compelling reason. It must be shown to have harmed the child (Pablo-Gualberto v. Gualberto). Custody of the 5-year-old does not automatically go to the father.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. The action of the innocent spouse to revoke a donation made in favor of the offending spouse must be brought within five years from the time the decree of legal separation has become final.
2. The revocation of the designation of the offending spouse as beneficiary in an insurance policy takes effect upon the finality of the decree of legal separation.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: Art. 64 FC. No. 1 is TRUE: it is the last sentence of Art. 64. No. 2 is FALSE. The revocation of, or change in, the insurance beneficiary designation 'shall take effect upon WRITTEN NOTIFICATION thereof to the insured,' not upon finality of the decree. Revocation is also optional on the innocent spouse's part.

stem: While their action for legal separation was being tried, H and W reconciled. What is the proper procedure and its effect?
choices: They shall file a joint manifestation under oath, duly signed by them, in the same proceeding, and the proceedings shall be terminated at whatever stage
They shall file a new petition to set aside the action, and the court shall terminate the proceedings only after hearing
Either of them may file a unilateral manifestation of reconciliation, and the case shall be archived
The court shall suspend the proceedings for six months to verify the reconciliation
None of the above
explanation: Art. 65 FC: upon reconciliation, the spouses file a joint manifestation under oath, duly signed by them, in the same proceeding. Art. 66(1): the proceedings, if still pending, 'shall thereby be terminated at whatever stage.' No decree issues, and no court approval of the reconciliation is needed to terminate the case. (d) is wrong: the six-month period has nothing to do with reconciliation.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. If the spouses reconcile after the decree of legal separation has become final, the separation of property and any forfeiture of the share of the guilty spouse already effected shall subsist, unless the spouses agree to revive their former property regime.
2. The agreement to revive the former property regime need not be approved by the court, as long as it is executed under oath and copies are furnished to the creditors named therein.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is Art. 66(2) FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Under Art. 67, the agreement must be under oath and specify the properties contributed anew, those retained as separate property, and all known creditors. It must be filed with a motion for its approval in the same proceeding, with copies furnished to the creditors. After due hearing, the COURT approves it in an order that protects creditors and is recorded in the proper registries of property.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. Where violence as defined in the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act is alleged in a petition for legal separation, the six-month cooling-off period shall not apply.

2. If the petitioner dies after the case has been submitted for decision, the court may still render a decree of legal separation because the action also affects the property relations of the spouses.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE. RA 9262 (Anti-VAWC Act), Sec. 19: 'In cases of legal separation, where violence as specified in this Act is alleged, Article 58 of the Family Code shall not apply. The court shall proceed on the main case and other incidents of the case as soon as possible.' No. 2 is FALSE. An action for legal separation is purely personal, and the death of a party before the decree becomes final abates the action, even if it had been submitted for decision (Lapuz-Sy v. Eufemio). The property consequences of the death are settled in the estate proceedings, not by a posthumous decree.

stem: W left the conjugal abode without just cause. H filed a petition asking the court to compel W, under pain of contempt, to return to the conjugal abode and perform her marital obligations. The petition will prosper.
choices: True
False
explanation: No. The obligation to live together (Art. 68 FC) cannot be enforced by compulsion. In Arroyo v. Vasquez de Arroyo, the Supreme Court held that it is not within the province of the courts to compel one spouse to cohabit with the other. An order enforceable by contempt may not be issued to restore the purely personal right of consortium, even if the wife left without just cause. The sanctions are patrimonial and indirect: loss of the right to support (Art. 100(1)/127(1)), legal separation if the abandonment exceeds one year (Art. 55(10)), and judicial separation of property (Arts. 101, 135).

stem: If the wife left the conjugal abode:
choices: The court can compel her to live with her husband under pain of contempt.
The court can compel her to live with her husband under pain of contempt only if she left the conjugal abode without just cause.
The husband may still be compelled to give support.
The husband can be compelled to give support even if the abandonment was without just cause.
None of the above.
explanation: (a) and (b) are wrong. Courts will not compel cohabitation by contempt, whether or not the wife left with just cause (Arroyo v. Vasquez de Arroyo; Ilusorio v. Bildner as to habeas corpus). (c) is correct: if the wife left with just cause, for example because of maltreatment or the husband's base demands, the husband may still be compelled to support her outside the conjugal home (Goitia v. Campos-Rueda). (d) is wrong: under Arts. 100(1) and 127(1) FC, the spouse who leaves the conjugal home without just cause has no right to be supported.
