stem: The family domicile shall be fixed by:
choices: the husband
the wife
the husband and wife. in case of disagreement, the husband's decision shall prevail.
the husband and wife. in case of disagreement, the family council shall decide.
the husband and wife. in case of disagreement, the court shall decide.
explanation: Art. 69 FC: 'The husband and wife shall fix the family domicile. In case of disagreement, the COURT shall decide.' Choice (c), where the husband's decision prevails, was the Civil Code rule (Art. 110), which the Family Code abolished in favor of equality of the spouses. There is no family council or 'family court' rule in Art. 69.
key_note: Note: two samplex keys (old Quiz No. 3 and Leviathan Quiz 3) marked (c). This is incorrect because (c) states the repealed Civil Code rule; Art. 69 FC leaves disagreements to the court.

stem: The husband’s acts of forcibly ejecting his wife without just cause from the conjugal dwelling and refusing to take her back constitutes:
choices: desertion.
recrimination.
constructive abandonment.
de facto separation.
explanation: When a husband, without just cause, forcibly ejects his wife from the conjugal dwelling and refuses to take her back, it is HE who is deemed to have abandoned the marriage. This is constructive abandonment, even though she is the one who physically left. In De la Viña v. Villareal, the wife may acquire a separate domicile when the husband unlawfully ejects her. She is not the deserting spouse and keeps her right to support (cf. Arts. 100(1), 101 FC). Recrimination is a defense in legal separation, and de facto separation is merely the fact of living apart.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. A promise by a husband to pay his wife money if she will continue to cohabit with him is valid and enforceable, since it is supported by a valuable consideration.
2. The husband and wife are obligated to live together, observe mutual love, respect and fidelity, and render mutual help and support.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Tolentino: a husband's promise to pay his wife if she will cohabit with him or permit marital relations is void for want of cause or consideration, since she would be doing only what the law already obliges her to do. No. 2 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 68 FC.

stem: W left the conjugal home without justifiable cause. H filed an action asking the court to order W to return to the conjugal dwelling and to cohabit with him, under pain of contempt. The court should:
choices: Decline to compel W to cohabit with H by force or contempt, although W, having left without justification, may be denied support
Order the police to bring W back to the conjugal dwelling
Order W to return, enforceable by contempt proceedings
Decree legal separation motu proprio
None of the above
explanation: Arts. 68, 72 FC. Cohabitation must be spontaneous. Courts will not compel a spouse to live with the other by force or contempt (Arroyo v. Vasquez de Arroyo, 42 Phil. 54), and Tolentino believes the Arroyo doctrine survives Art. 72. The sanction is patrimonial. A spouse who leaves the conjugal home without just cause loses the right to be supported (Arts. 100(1), 127(1)).

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. A husband may compel his wife to have sexual intercourse against her will, since the right to sexual relations is absolute in marriage.
2. Any person who interferes with the right of the spouses to cohabitation may be held liable for damages under Article 26 of the Civil Code.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Tolentino: the right to marital relations is not absolute. The wife may justly refuse, for example when the husband demands abnormal acts or has a venereal disease (Goitia v. Campos-Rueda). Marital rape is punishable under the Anti-Rape Law (RA 8353). No. 2 is TRUE. A third person who interferes with the spouses' right to cohabitation may be liable for damages under Art. 26 Civil Code (Tolentino).

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. The husband and wife shall fix the family domicile; in case of disagreement, the court shall decide.
2. The court may exempt one spouse from living with the other if the latter should live abroad, even if such exemption is not compatible with the solidarity of the family.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is Art. 69, first paragraph, FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Art. 69 allows the court to exempt one spouse from living with the other if the latter lives abroad or there are other valid and compelling reasons, but 'such exemption shall NOT apply if the same is not compatible with the solidarity of the family.'

stem: Under Article 70, the expenses for the support of the family and other conjugal obligations shall be paid:
choices: First from the separate properties of the spouses, then from the community property

From the community property, and in the absence thereof, from the income or fruits of their separate properties; in case of insufficiency or absence of said income or fruits, from their separate properties
Exclusively by the husband, as head of the family
Equally by the spouses from their separate properties regardless of the value thereof
None of the above
explanation: Verbatim Art. 70 FC. The spouses are jointly responsible for the support of the family. Expenses are paid first from the community property, then from the income or fruits of their separate properties, and if that is insufficient or absent, from the separate properties themselves. The Civil Code made the husband primarily responsible.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. The management of the household shall be the right and duty of the wife, and in case of disagreement the court shall decide.

2. When one of the spouses neglects his or her duties to the conjugal union or commits acts which tend to bring danger, dishonor or injury to the other or to the family, the aggrieved party may apply to the court for relief.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Art. 71 FC: management of the household is the right and duty of BOTH spouses, and the expenses are paid according to Art. 70. The provision says nothing about court resolution of disagreements, and it does not assign household management to the wife alone. No. 2 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 72.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. The other spouse may object to the exercise of such profession, occupation, business or activity on any ground which, in his or her judgment, would serve the interest of the family.
2. Either spouse may exercise any legitimate profession, occupation, business or activity without the consent of the other.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is FALSE. Under Art. 73 FC, the other spouse may object ONLY on 'valid, serious, and moral grounds,' not on any ground he or she deems to serve the family. No. 2 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 73, first sentence. Tolentino calls the objection a 'conditional veto' based on unity of direction. In case of disagreement, the court decides whether the objection is proper.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. The husband and wife are obliged to live together, observe mutual love, respect and fidelity, and render mutual help and support.
2. The obligation of mutual fidelity between the spouses ceases upon the filing of a petition for legal separation.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 68 FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Filing the petition only entitles the spouses to live separately (Art. 61). Even the decree does not sever the marriage bond (Art. 63(1)), so the obligation of fidelity continues, and adultery or concubinage committed during the case or after the decree remains punishable.

stem: E, the wife, filed a petition for habeas corpus to have custody of her husband P, an elderly but mentally competent man, who had chosen to live apart from her in his own condominium unit. The court should:
choices: Grant the writ, since the wife has the right to the society of her husband under Article 68
Grant the writ but allow P to choose where the spouses shall live
Deny the writ, since habeas corpus may not be used to enforce marital rights such as cohabitation, and there is no illegal restraint of P
Deny the writ but grant E visitation rights enforceable by contempt
None of the above
explanation: Ilusorio v. Bildner: a writ of habeas corpus may not be used to compel a husband to live with his wife. Marital rights, including coverture and living in the conjugal dwelling, cannot be enforced by habeas corpus. The writ lies only against illegal restraint of liberty, and a competent husband freely choosing where to live is not restrained. The Court also struck down the visitation rights granted to the wife, because they forced him to be visited against his will and violated his privacy. This follows Arroyo v. Vasquez de Arroyo, under which courts will not compel cohabitation.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. A wife who was compelled to leave the conjugal dwelling because of her husband's maltreatment may claim support from him even if she lives elsewhere and no action for legal separation has been filed.
2. The husband may always fulfill his obligation to support his wife, at his option, by receiving and maintaining her in the family dwelling.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE. Goitia v. Campos-Rueda: a wife forced to leave the conjugal home because of the husband's base demands and maltreatment may claim support from him outside it. The obligation of support does not depend on divorce or legal separation. No. 2 is FALSE. The obligor's option to give support by receiving and maintaining the recipient in the family dwelling 'cannot be availed of in case there is a moral or legal obstacle thereto' (Art. 204 FC). The husband who made cohabitation intolerable cannot invoke it.

stem: H, a career diplomat, was assigned to an embassy abroad. W refused to join him, preferring to remain in Manila where she runs a business and the children study. H filed a petition asking the court to require W to live with him abroad. Under Article 69:
choices: The court may exempt W from living with H because he lives abroad, unless the exemption is not compatible with the solidarity of the family
W must follow H, since the husband fixes the family domicile
W is automatically exempt from living with H since he lives abroad
The court may order W, under pain of contempt, to live with H abroad
None of the above
explanation: Art. 69 FC: the court MAY exempt one spouse from living with the other if the latter should live abroad or there are other valid and compelling reasons. However, the exemption 'shall not apply if the same is not compatible with the solidarity of the family.' The exemption is discretionary, not automatic (Tolentino). The husband's choice does not prevail under the FC, and the wife cannot be compelled to cohabit.

stem: Under the Family Code, in case of disagreement between the spouses as to the family domicile, the decision of the husband shall prevail, subject to the wife's recourse to the court.
choices: True
False
explanation: Under Art. 110 of the Civil Code, the husband fixed the residence of the family, and the court could exempt the wife from living with him only if he lived abroad (unless in the service of the Republic). Art. 69 FC replaced this with joint authority: 'The husband and wife shall fix the family domicile. In case of disagreement, the court shall decide.' The husband's decision no longer prevails.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. The spouses are jointly responsible for the support of the family.

2. In the absence of community property, the expenses for the support of the family shall be paid directly from the separate properties of the spouses, the income or fruits thereof being reached only if the separate properties are insufficient.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is Art. 70, first sentence, FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Art. 70 sets the order: (1) community property; (2) in its absence, the INCOME OR FRUITS of the separate properties; (3) only in case of insufficiency or absence of those income or fruits, the separate properties themselves. The fruits of separate property come before the capital.

stem: The management of the household shall be the right and the duty of both spouses, and the expenses for such management shall be paid first from the separate properties of the spouses.
choices: True
False
explanation: Art. 71 FC: the management of the household is the right and duty of BOTH spouses (this part is correct), and the expenses 'shall be paid in accordance with the provisions of Article 70': first from community property, then from the income or fruits of separate properties, then from the separate properties. They are not paid first from the separate properties, so the statement is not absolutely true.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. When one of the spouses neglects his or her duties to the conjugal union or commits acts which tend to bring danger, dishonor or injury to the other or to the family, the aggrieved party may apply to the court for relief.
2. Under Article 72, the court may order the erring spouse, under pain of contempt, to resume cohabitation with the aggrieved spouse.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is verbatim Art. 72 FC. No. 2 is FALSE. Tolentino: the court may grant any LAWFUL relief, such as support, judicial separation of property, receivership, or legal separation if a ground exists. It cannot use coercive force to make a spouse perform a purely personal act such as cohabitation, and the Arroyo v. Vasquez doctrine still stands.

stem: H habitually gambles away the family's funds and neglects to provide for W and the children. W does not want legal separation. Which is correct?
choices: W may apply to the court for relief under Article 72
W has no remedy unless she files for legal separation
W may seek relief only if H has been sentenced by final judgment to imprisonment of more than six years
W must first bring the matter before the family council
None of the above
explanation: Art. 72 FC lets the aggrieved spouse 'apply to the court for relief' when the other neglects his duties to the conjugal union or commits acts that bring danger, dishonor or injury to the family. Habitual gambling away of family funds is such an act. Tolentino: the court may grant any lawful relief, such as an order of support, separation of property or receivership. (b) is wrong because Art. 72 is an independent remedy. (c) is wrong because a sentence of more than six years (Art. 55(4)) has nothing to do with this remedy. (d) is wrong because the FC has no family council.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. If the court finds that benefit accrued to the family prior to the other spouse's objection to the exercise of a profession, the resulting obligation shall be enforced against the community property.
2. If the benefit accrued after the objection, the resulting obligation shall likewise be enforced against the community property, without prejudice to reimbursement.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: Art. 73 FC. (This is the text as amended by RA 10572 (2013). The original 1987 text, as printed in Tolentino, charged obligations from benefits accrued before the objection to the separate property of the non-consenting spouse; RA 10572 rewrote that clause. Answer under the amended text.) No. 1 is TRUE: if the benefit accrued to the family PRIOR to the objection, the resulting obligation is enforced against the COMMUNITY property. No. 2 is FALSE: if the benefit accrued THEREAFTER, the obligation is enforced against the SEPARATE property of the spouse who has not obtained consent.

stem: The rules under Article 73 on the enforcement of obligations arising from a spouse's profession or business against the community property or the separate property of the spouse who has not obtained consent shall not prejudice the rights of creditors who acted in good faith.
choices: True
False
explanation: Verbatim Art. 73, last paragraph, FC: 'The foregoing provisions shall not prejudice the rights of creditors who acted in good faith.' Third persons who dealt in good faith with the spouse exercising the profession or business, without knowledge of the objection, are protected.

stem: When the spouses disagree about the exercise by one of them of a profession or business, the court shall decide whether or not:
choices: The objection is proper
Benefit has accrued to the family prior to the objection or thereafter
Both of the above
The parents and grandparents of the spouses consent to the exercise of the profession
None of the above
explanation: Art. 73 FC: 'In case of disagreement, the court shall decide whether or not: (1) the objection is proper, and (2) benefit has accrued to the family prior to the objection or thereafter.' Both (a) and (b) are therefore matters for the court. The consultation with parents, grandparents and the family council in (d) was the Civil Code rule (Art. 117), and the FC dropped it.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. In case of separation in fact, the spouse who leaves the conjugal home or refuses to live therein, without just cause, shall not have the right to be supported.
2. In case of separation in fact, when the consent of one spouse to any transaction of the other is required by law, such consent is dispensed with.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is Art. 100(1) FC (Art. 127(1) for the CPG). No. 2 is FALSE. Under Art. 100(2) / 127(2), when one spouse's consent to a transaction of the other is required by law during a separation in fact, 'judicial authorization shall be obtained in a summary proceeding.' The consent is not dispensed with.

stem: H and W, married under the absolute community regime, have been separated in fact for two years. The community property is insufficient to support the family. Under Article 100:
choices: Only H, as the spouse who left, is liable for the support of the family from his separate property
The separate properties of both spouses shall be solidarily liable for the support of the family
The obligation to support the family is suspended during the separation in fact
W must first file a petition for legal separation before she can reach H's separate property
None of the above
explanation: Art. 100(3) FC (Art. 127(3) for CPG): during a separation in fact, 'in the absence of sufficient community property, the separate property of both spouses shall be SOLIDARILY liable for the support of the family.' The spouse present may, upon petition in a summary proceeding, be given judicial authority to administer or encumber specific separate property of the other spouse and use the fruits or proceeds to satisfy the latter's share.

stem: Consider the statement true only when it is absolutely true.
statements: 1. A spouse who has left the conjugal dwelling for a period of three months or has failed within the same period to give any information as to his or her whereabouts shall be prima facie presumed to have no intention of returning to the conjugal dwelling.
2. Such absence for three months is, by itself, a ground for legal separation.
choices: Both are true
Both are false
No. 1 is true, No. 2 is false
No. 1 is false, No. 2 is true
explanation: No. 1 is TRUE: it is Art. 101, third paragraph, FC. No. 2 is FALSE. The three-month presumption is relevant to the remedies under Art. 101 (receivership, judicial separation of property, sole administration). As a ground for legal separation, abandonment must be WITHOUT JUSTIFIABLE CAUSE and must last for MORE THAN ONE YEAR (Art. 55(10)).

stem: W left the conjugal home without just cause and refuses to return. Which of the following is available to H?
choices: H may refuse to give W support while she remains away without just cause
H may file for legal separation if the abandonment without justifiable cause lasts for more than one year
H may obtain a writ of habeas corpus to bring W back to the conjugal home
Both (a) and (b)
All of the above
explanation: Cohabitation cannot be compelled, whether by contempt (Arroyo v. Vasquez de Arroyo) or by habeas corpus (Ilusorio v. Bildner). The law's sanctions are patrimonial and indirect. Under Arts. 100(1) and 127(1) FC, the spouse who leaves without just cause has no right to be supported. If the abandonment without justifiable cause lasts more than one year, it becomes a ground for legal separation (Art. 55(10)). Both (a) and (b) are therefore correct.

stem: The essential marital obligations contemplated in Article 36 of the Family Code include those embraced by Articles 68 up to 71 of the Family Code.
choices: True
False
explanation: Republic v. Molina (guideline 6): the essential marital obligations under Art. 36 FC are those embraced by Arts. 68 up to 71 (the rights and obligations of spouses) and Arts. 220, 221 and 225 (obligations toward children). Under Tan-Andal v. Andal (2021), mere failure or refusal to perform these obligations is not psychological incapacity unless it results from a durable personality structure existing at the time of the celebration.

stem: H repeatedly demanded that W perform perverse sexual acts and maltreated her when she refused, so W left and stayed with her parents. W then sued H for support. H's defense is that he is willing to support her only if she returns to the conjugal home. Decide.
choices: W's action fails, because the husband has the option to support her in the conjugal dwelling
W's action fails, because she must first obtain a decree of legal separation
W is entitled to support outside the conjugal dwelling, because H's conduct is a moral and legal obstacle to his option to maintain her in the family dwelling
W is entitled to support only if she proves H's conduct in a criminal case
None of the above
explanation: Goitia v. Campos-Rueda: where the husband's demands for perverse acts and his maltreatment force the wife to leave, she may sue for support and receive it outside the conjugal home. The husband cannot insist on giving support only in the family dwelling, because there is a moral and legal obstacle (now Art. 204 FC). She need not first obtain legal separation, since the obligation flows from the subsisting marriage (Arts. 68, 195(1)). She left with just cause, so Art. 100(1)/127(1) does not bar her claim.
